transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-04
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jesse Park, Priya Menon, Ethan Li (Redwood) - Maya Chen, Liam O'Neill, Sabrina Patel, Noah Reyes (BlueDen)

Summary (auto): quick QBR/handoff to operations, go over economics and operational playbook, decide pilot cadence, agree owners.

[00:00] Jesse Park: okay everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Jesse from Redwood, i think we have Priya and Ethan on the call as well. how's everybody doing?
[00:08] Maya Chen: good thanks, Maya here. We wanted this call to lock down the rollout playbook and get a sense of the cost tradeoffs.
[00:15] Liam O'Neill: yep, and we want to make sure the SREs have a clear rollback plan for model rollouts so we don't panic friday nights.
[00:22] Priya Menon: got it. quick agenda, review last quarter usage, point out cost drivers, go over p95/p99 tail latency, then Dedicated sizing options and security items - k yes?
[00:35] Sabrina Patel: please include audit logging and KMS scoping early. we need to inventory what stays in our KMS versus what Redwood manages.
[00:44] Jesse Park: totally. quick housekeeping, the transcript might have some small audio artifacts, sorry if names get munged.

-- Usage and cost --
[01:05] Ethan Li: looking at the last 90 days, BlueDen ran roughly 22M tokens per day average, peaks at 45M tokens across peak runs. Most cost is from long form generation where sequence lengths average 1,400 tokens.
[01:25] Maya Chen: that matches what we saw, the long-form summaries are the thing. also multiple model variants in test traffic spikes.
[01:33] Liam O'Neill: curious - what's our p95 for hosted v Dedicated in Redwood's benchmarks?
[01:39] Priya Menon: in our internal profiles for similar seq lengths, hosted p95 is about 320-380ms for the redwood-34B-ish family on gpus with our batch settings, Dedicated tuned can get p95 into the 220-280ms range with prefix KV caching and continuous batching. numbers vary with concurrency and KV cache hit rate.
[01:58] Maya Chen: okay so that's significant. if we go Dedicated for predictability, what's the unit cost delta?
[02:04] Jesse Park: ballpark, Dedicated commits reduce per-token compute ops by about 18-28% relative to on-demand hosted for sustained workloads; but there is a fixed monthly capacity fee that you need to weigh against bursty usage. We'll send a spreadsheet.
[02:20] Noah Reyes: can we get an example run for our traffic shape? we prefer to see end-to-end numbers not just per-token.
[02:27] Jesse Park: yes, action item - we'll run a cost model using your 7 days of logs.

-- Stability, tails, and incident guards --
[03:10] Liam O'Neill: last month we saw tail latency bursts at p99 during a traffic spike, traced to cold KV cache and a backend watermark. how does Redwood handle cache cold starts? any automatic pre-warm?
[03:23] Priya Menon: we do prefix caching and K/V cache retention. there's a cache warming option for Dedicated where hot prefixes are pinned to the pool, that reduces cold miss rate. Also we have circuit-breaker fallbacks to a smaller faster variant if the main model crosses an error rate threshold.
[03:43] Maya Chen: is fallback automatic or do we control policy?
[03:47] Priya Menon: policy driven - you set latency SLOs and fallback windows. We'll demonstrate in the pilot.

-- Security & Compliance --
[04:10] Sabrina Patel: quick note from security: we need to confirm where logs live, retention windows, and whether Redwood can push audit logs to our SIEM. also KMS: do you wrap sessions in our HSM or hold keys?
[04:22] Jesse Park: for Private/VPC deployments customers can bring their own KMS; for Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations. We can stream audit logs to a customer-owned endpoint or provide syslog/s3 exports. we'll send the SOC2 appendix.
[04:36] Sabrina Patel: great, also are you able to provide per-request token-level billing artifacts? our finance team needs mapping to internal chargeback.
[04:45] Ethan Li: yes we have token-level trace IDs and cost-breakdown per route, we can map that to account ids for your chargeback.

-- Pilot scope and rollouts --
[05:10] Jesse Park: propose pilot: two-week Dedicated reservation with a smaller pool (baseline), run traffic replay for 48 hours for stress, then gradual live traffic rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with canary and automatic rollback on error/latency thresholds.
[05:25] Noah Reyes: timeline question - we have internal windows for maintenance 11/20-11/22, prefer pilot start earlier.
[05:31] Jesse Park: ok we can propose kickoff 11/17 and schedule the 48-hour benchmark 11/10 as SE run.

[06:00] Priya Menon: technical nit - when we run the benchmark we'll include KV hit/miss heatmaps, batch sizes distribution, GPU utilization, and memory pressure. that helps pick the quant profile that minimizes dequant latency.
[06:14] Liam O'Neill: what's 'dequant latency' again?
[06:17] Priya Menon: sorry shorthand - if we use int8 or 4-bit quantization, there's a minor decompression or conversion cost per token; some kernels incur higher per-token overhead at short sequences. we include that in the benchmark so it's not a surprise.

-- Deep tradeoffs: batching vs latency --
[07:05] Maya Chen: earlier we tried aggressive batching but some critical chat flows need <200ms. how do you balance?
[07:12] Priya Menon: Redwood supports route-level config: low-latency routes can pin to smaller batch windows and lower packing. We also support hybrid routing: critical traffic to Dedicated low-latency pool, bulk to batch-optimized capacity.
[07:27] Jesse Park: to add, caching reduces per-token compute regardless of batch; so for long sequences the caching benefit is bigger.

-- Pricing details asked --
[08:00] Maya Chen: finance will want line items for committed cost, per-token variable, and observability add-on.
[08:06] Jesse Park: we'll provide the pricing sheet with those line items broken out and a few example scenarios.

-- Questions from customer --
[09:00] Maya Chen: two quick ones - 1) can Dedicated be colocated in our EU region? 2) what happens if we exceed commit in a month?
[09:07] Priya Menon: 1) yes, we have region options for Dedicated; 2) we have burst capacity and/or per-token overage billing; we'll map the commit and burst policy in the proposal.

[09:30] Sabrina Patel: are there any regulatory controls we need to be aware of for data residency?
[09:35] Jesse Park: for Private we can do on-prem or VPC; audit logs can remain inside your tenancy. We have guidance docs; we'll attach the residency appendix.

-- Mid-call recap --
[10:00] Jesse Park: recap, we will: share pricing by 11/09, SE run benchmark 11/10-11/11, security packet by 11/06, pilot kickoff propose 11/17. any objections?
[10:12] all: nope

-- Transcript middle (benchmarks and metrics deep-dive) --
[12:00] Priya Menon: for the benchmark, please expect charts: token distribution, seq length histogram, p50/p95/p99 over time, and KV cache hit heatmaps, also kernel selection notes per model variant. we'll include recommended quantization profiles.
[12:25] Liam O'Neill: on kernel selection, are you using Triton or custom kernels?
[12:28] Priya Menon: mix - runtime will select optimized kernels and sometimes custom fused kernels for attention. we also tune based on sequence length distribution.
[12:38] Maya Chen: ok fine. Also want to call out logging overhead, in our tests enabling full debug and token-level logging added an extra ~12% latency.
[12:50] Ethan Li: noted - we'll add that to the benchmark matrix as 'obs-on vs obs-off'.

-- Edge cases and failure modes --
[15:00] Noah Reyes: what's the behavior when a model crashes mid-request? we need graceful degradation.
[15:05] Priya Menon: our runtime can truncate and fail-safe to a fallback model; we also surface error metadata for automatic retries. We recommend idempotency keys on the client to avoid duplicates.
[15:16] Liam O'Neill: would an automatic fallback cause a cost spike?
[15:19] Jesse Park: minimal for short fallbacks - the fallback model is smaller and cheaper. biggest risk is if repeated retries occur; that's why we have circuit-breakers.

-- Observability and Console --
[18:10] Ethan Li: demo note - Console exposes route-level token burn, latency histograms, per-client tracing. We'll share a read-only link for BlueDen's dev account during pilot.
[18:20] Maya Chen: we need role-based access - devs should not see production keys.
[18:24] Jesse Park: RBAC is supported, SSO via SAML or OIDC. We'll map roles in the runbook.

-- Pricing scenarios discussion --
[21:00] Jesse Park: scenario A - hosted with burst: low fixed cost, higher per-token; Scenario B - Dedicated commit: higher fixed, lower per-token; Scenario C - Private/VPC: enterprise fee plus managed support. We'll send a spreadsheet with three scenarios and thresholds.
[21:22] Maya Chen: prefer to evaluate scenario B if the projected 6-month run rate sustains the commit.

-- Objections and clarifications --
[24:00] Sabrina Patel: any concerns about vendor lock-in? we want exit strategy.
[24:07] Priya Menon: we support model artifacts export and KV cache snapshots; you can export the model and data. We'll document the offboarding steps.

-- End of meeting recap and owners --
[55:00] Jesse Park: final recap and owners - Priya SE owns benchmark, Jesse owns pricing and pilot terms, Sabrina to send security constraints, Noah to share staging routes. We'll follow up with calendar invites.
[55:20] Maya Chen: thanks, appreciate the clear owners.
[55:30] Liam O'Neill: small ask - can you include a short runbook for on-call SREs during rollout? just steps to toggle traffic and read the console quick metrics.
[55:40] Priya Menon: yes, we'll include an on-call cheat sheet as part of the pilot docs.
[56:00] Jesse Park: perfect, we'll get notes out and action items in CRM. thanks everyone.
[56:10] Sabrina Patel: thanks all, bye.

End of transcript.
